site_surface.short_summary: Esper is a live-pilot Alara shard expression for Blue-centered perfectibility through knowledge, planning, ordered improvement, and focused control.
site_surface.one_sentence_identity: Esper asks whether a world can be improved by making change deliberate, structured, and information-led.
best_for: users drawn to planning, knowledge, and structured control
Commander language around control, card advantage, library care, and artifact-oriented value
players who prefer optimization as a deliberate design project
content_warnings_or_sensitivity_notes: Esper material can involve hierarchy, control, body modification themes, war, and deferred story material. This packet does not narrate those details as current claims.

core_identity.summary: Esper is the Blue-centered white-blue-black Alara shard in which perfectibility is modeled through knowledge, planning, applied information, ordered improvement, and focused control.
core_identity.philosophy: Blue supplies the center: potential can be unlocked through knowledge and deliberate change. White gives the improvement project structure and coordination. Black gives the project focus, ambition, and the will to make information useful.
core_identity.central_tension: Vox Mana models Esper's tension as perfectibility drifting into over-control, where the unoptimized starts to look like an error to correct.
core_identity.interpretive_note: The central tension and Commander-facing language are Vox Mana modeling from the promoted evidence floor, not official Wizards or MTG canon.

great_tension.summary: Vox Mana models Esper's great tension as perfectibility becoming over-control: a design project that can forget the difference between improving a system and treating life as a defect.
great_tension.placement_relevance: Use as live-pilot placement guidance only when the answer combines Blue-centered perfectibility, White ordered improvement, and Black focused control. Do not use detailed lore, generic three-color control, or color identity alone as routing evidence.

commander_compass.recommendation_philosophy: Use Esper Commander guidance as product/operator support: exact White/Blue/Black decks can express planning, control, card advantage, library setup, lifegain engines, artifact-oriented value, and precise combat lines. These rows do not create Esper canon, geography, story, metallurgy, named-figure, or raw claims.

native_fit_commanders.why_this_fits: Scions & Spellcraft is an exact White/Blue/Black support deck, and Y'shtola turns answers and card flow into a steady advantage plan that fits Esper's knowledge-first control lane.
native_fit_commanders.skip_if: The player wants fast combat, low bookkeeping, or Alaran Esper story grounding.
native_fit_commanders.gameplay_summary: Keep answers ready, draw through the table's pressure, and let each exchange become another piece of controlled advantage.
caution_notes: Product/operator support; not Esper canon evidence.
Do not treat crossover story context as Alaran Esper lore.

native_fit_commanders.why_this_fits: Miracle Worker is exact White/Blue/Black support, and Aminatou rewards library setup, enchantment engines, and perfectly timed miracle turns.
native_fit_commanders.skip_if: The player dislikes topdeck planning, enchantment engines, or careful sequencing.
native_fit_commanders.gameplay_summary: Arrange the top of the library, make the answer cheaper at the right moment, and let planning turn into tempo.
caution_notes: Product/operator support; not Esper canon evidence.

native_fit_commanders.why_this_fits: Eternal Bargain is exact White/Blue/Black support, and Oloro turns life gain, card draw, and artifact value into a slow plan of inevitability.
native_fit_commanders.skip_if: The player wants proactive combat or dislikes a slower command-zone engine.
native_fit_commanders.gameplay_summary: Convert time and life totals into cards, then use those cards to control when the table can move.
caution_notes: Product/operator support; not Esper canon evidence.

weird_stretch_commanders.why_this_fits: Obscura Operation is exact White/Blue/Black support, and Kamiz shows Esper as precise evasive pressure rather than a pure control shell.
weird_stretch_commanders.skip_if: The player wants classic draw-go control, no combat focus, or New Capenna identity treated as Alaran Esper.
weird_stretch_commanders.gameplay_summary: Choose the threat that must connect, protect its line, and let each hit improve the next decision.
caution_notes: Same-color product support; not Esper canon evidence.
Do not display as a lore-forward Alara recommendation.

advanced_complexity_commanders.why_this_fits: Subjective Reality is exact White/Blue/Black support, and Aminatou rewards top-of-library setup, blink value, and deliberately chosen draws.
advanced_complexity_commanders.skip_if: The player wants simple combat math or dislikes managing the top card of the library.
advanced_complexity_commanders.gameplay_summary: Set the next draw, blink the right permanent, and let the table feel every future line become curated.
caution_notes: Product/operator support; not Esper canon evidence.

advanced_complexity_commanders.why_this_fits: Urza's Iron Alliance is exact White/Blue/Black support, and Urza turns artifact creatures and token production into a designed board state.
advanced_complexity_commanders.skip_if: The player wants spell control with few permanents or wants artifact lore treated as Esper proof.
advanced_complexity_commanders.gameplay_summary: Build the artifact board piece by piece, then make the machine attack as one planned system.
caution_notes: Product/operator support; not Esper canon evidence.
Keep artifacts as gameplay texture rather than material-lore proof.

archetype_lanes.description: Keep answers ready, convert cards into options, and make each exchange narrow the table's future.
archetype_lanes.recommended_for: Y'shtola, Night's Blessed; Oloro, Ageless Ascetic
archetype_lanes.skip_if: The player wants fast combat or minimal stack interaction.

archetype_lanes.description: Use top-of-library setup, miracles, blink value, and selected draws to make planning feel material.
archetype_lanes.recommended_for: Aminatou, Veil Piercer; Aminatou, the Fateshifter
archetype_lanes.skip_if: The player dislikes sequencing or managing hidden information.

archetype_lanes.description: Use artifact value, tokens, and board construction as gameplay support for structured optimization.
archetype_lanes.skip_if: The player wants artifact lore treated as proof of Esper canon.

archetype_lanes.description: Use evasive pressure, connive, Knights, or formation play when Esper should feel exact rather than purely defensive.
archetype_lanes.recommended_for: Sidar Jabari of Zhalfir; Kamiz, Obscura Oculus
archetype_lanes.skip_if: The player wants draw-go control with little combat.
